charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

affo.title: AFFO
affo.content:
AFFO (adjusted funds from operations) is a property owner's distributable cash: net income excluding revaluations, adjusted for maintenance capex and lease incentives.

For The GPT Group: the valuation capitalises AFFO at the cost of equity; statutory net income is dominated by revaluation noise.

What to watch:

  • AFFO per share growth
  • Payout ratio (DPS / AFFO per share)

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For The GPT Group: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For The GPT Group: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For The GPT Group: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

ffo.title: FFO
ffo.content:
FFO (funds from operations) is the REIT-industry standard earnings measure: statutory net income with non-cash investment-property revaluations and other fair-value movements added back.

For The GPT Group: the DCF capitalises FFO/AFFO, not statutory NPAT — net income swings with revaluation gains and losses that never turn into distributable cash. FFO has full history back to FY2019 (H1 back to FY2015); AFFO, which further deducts maintenance capex and leasing incentives, is only disclosed from H1 FY2023.

What to watch:

  • FFO per security growth versus distribution per security (payout ratio)
  • FFO trend versus statutory net income — a widening gap means revaluations are doing more of the reported work

netGearing.title: Net gearing
netGearing.content:
Net gearing is net debt as a percentage of total tangible assets (or an equivalent REIT-specific ratio disclosed by the company) — the leverage figure REIT investors and lenders watch directly, distinct from a raw debt/equity ratio.

For The GPT Group: gearing is the key risk flagged in the qualitative analysis — a REIT's covenant headroom and refinancing capacity both hinge on it, and it moves with investment-property valuations as well as borrowings. FY2025 gearing stepped up to the low-30s% from the mid-20s%, the highest in the reported history.

What to watch:

  • Gearing trending toward covenant ceilings (typically ~45-50% for ASX REITs)
  • Whether an increase is from new borrowing or falling asset valuations

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For The GPT Group: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

occupancy.title: Occupancy
occupancy.content:
The share of lettable space (or units) that is leased.

For The GPT Group: occupancy below the sector norm is the first sign of rental pressure.

What to watch:

  • Occupancy trend
  • Lease expiries in the next two years

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For The GPT Group: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For The GPT Group: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

rental.title: Gross rental income
rental.content:
Rent received from tenants before property expenses.

For The GPT Group: compare with AFFO to see how much of rent reaches owners.

What to watch:

  • Like-for-like rental growth

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For The GPT Group: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For The GPT Group: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
